name: orla
description: Bookkeeping for growing businesses and people: your assistant books a bank statement after you check the rows, sorts expenses, drafts invoices, shows what a month needs to close. No money moves.

interface.longDescription:
Hand your assistant a bank statement (PDF, photo or CSV): it shows the rows it would book, why any would not and whether the printed balances add up, then books exactly those after your yes. Then ask what the month lacks: payments with no document, bills waiting, whether it is ready to close.

Orla keeps the books for growing businesses and people whose money sits in banks, cards, cash and crypto.

What it can read: accounts and last sync, transactions, categories, budgets, net worth, goals, contacts, invoices, supplier bills (flagged on new bank details or a likely duplicate), and Orla's reports: spending, cash flow, VAT, loans, trial balance.

What it can record: a transaction and fixes to its category, payee, note or tags; a split; a category rule; a budget, a goal, a recurring payment; a contact; a file on a transaction; a supplier bill from a file, waiting for you to accept it; a bill paid outside Orla, tied to its bank row. A statement can be taken back out within 7 days. Changes to many rows are shown first. Amount, date and account cannot be edited.

It drafts invoices to your contacts and emails an invoice or reminder only as previewed, if you ticked that letter on the consent screen.

On paid plans: routines, questions Orla answers on a schedule by email or Telegram; and, if your assistant can read your mailbox, it lists a month of bills and receipts and, after one yes, forwards them to your space's bills address.

With Orla Pro: reconciliation, a request to close a ready month that you confirm in Orla, the investor update with its reconciliation status, and business reports.

It cannot move money: this connection has no payment, transfer or card tool.

On the consent screen you pick the spaces and whether card numbers, IBANs and wallet addresses show in full or masked (default).

A free account is enough. On Free: 50 recorded entries and 3 invoices a month, your first statement counts as one; reading a statement uses the AI allowance, about four a month.

positive.description: Net worth across the user's accounts
positive.expected_behavior: The answer gives the total and says how many accounts were left out and which currencies had no rate.

positive.prompt: Show my transactions from last month.
positive.expected_behavior: A long list comes back shortened, with the number returned and the real total.
Reports each budget against its limit.

positive.prompt: Record 12.50 EUR for coffee from my Cash account today.
positive.expected_behavior: Finds the Cash account, then books the expense; the entry lands in the books straight away.

positive.prompt: Where did my money go last month, by category?
positive.expected_behavior: Reads the spending by category report and answers from it.
